headline: Massachusetts Requires Giant Data Centers to Run on 100% Clean Energy
meta_description: Governor Maura Healey signed an executive order requiring large data centers to meet all electricity demand with renewable power they provide or fund themselve…
summary_short: Massachusetts data centers over 25 MW must now power themselves entirely with clean energy under a new executive order from Governor Maura Healey.
body:
Governor Maura Healey signed an executive order requiring data centers over 25 megawatts to meet 100% of their electricity demand with clean energy. The facilities must either provide the renewable power themselves or fund its development elsewhere.

This order addresses a growing challenge: as artificial intelligence and cloud computing expand, data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity, often straining regional power grids. By shifting this burden to clean sources, Massachusetts aims to support technological growth without sacrificing its climate commitments.

The requirement applies specifically to facilities exceeding the 25 MW threshold, making it substantial enough to drive real change while offering smaller operators more flexibility. The executive order represents a practical approach to aligning corporate expansion with renewable energy goals—companies wanting to operate in Massachusetts must invest in the clean power infrastructure the state needs.
quick_facts: Governor Maura Healey signed the executive order
Applies to data centers over 25 megawatts
Requires 100% clean electricity for covered facilities
Companies must provide or fund renewable power
